scenarios.name: single-tube-sff-comparison
scenarios.purpose: Compare Journey Planner's whole single-journey fare with FareTo for the same Tube station pair. Inspect raw values, ticket types, peak/off-peak fields, caveats and fare validity dates.

fareTo.purpose: Same station-pair FareTo comparison; do not infer universal equality from one match.

scenarios.name: multi-leg-tube-transfer
scenarios.purpose: Check that a route with an in-station Tube transfer can have multiple vehicle legs but one fare object. Compare a full pair query and inspect leg count separately from fare count.

fareTo.purpose: Whole Tube station-pair FareTo reference, not a quote for each leg.

scenarios.name: mixed-bus-and-tube
scenarios.purpose: Inspect a bus-plus-Tube itinerary. Compare Journey Planner's full-route fare with FareTo for the Tube station pair only. Do not add the two quotes unless the response proves their scopes are disjoint.

fareTo.purpose: Tube station-pair reference within a mixed-mode journey; not the whole journey price.

scenarios.name: consecutive-bus-hopper
scenarios.purpose: Resolved stop IDs for a bus-only route that previously returned multiple bus legs. Inspect Journey Planner totalCost, each fare object, isHopperFare, busRouteId and tap timestamps. Fare components are not vehicle legs.

fareTo.purpose: Probe FareTo with bus-stop IDs. An empty response means no FareTo quote was returned; it is not a zero fare.

scenarios.name: hammersmith-osi
scenarios.purpose: Use the resolved Hammersmith interchange ID. Confirm a Tube leg to Hammersmith H&C, a walking interchange to the District/Piccadilly station, a second Tube leg and the returned fare. Planner legs do not simulate card validation.

fareTo.purpose: Whole station-pair reference across the Hammersmith OSI.

scenarios.name: avoid-zone-one-via-highbury
scenarios.purpose: Compare FareTo default/alternative fare rows with a Journey Planner route constrained via Highbury & Islington. Check that the route actually uses the intended interchange and that the fare taps reflect it. The API does not prove a rider touched a pink reader.

fareTo.purpose: Whole station-pair FareTo query; inspect all route rows and pink-reader conditions.

scenarios.name: national-rail-fare-coverage
scenarios.purpose: Test a National Rail plus Elizabeth line route and check whether Journey Planner returns fare data. Compare with the Tube-only FareTo endpoint; an empty FareTo array or missing Journey Planner fare must be represented as unknown, never zero.

fareTo.purpose: Probe FareTo support for a National Rail station pair; do not infer support from HTTP 200 alone.

scenarios.name: weekday-peak-boundaries
scenarios.purpose: Compare requested times around published weekday fare boundaries. Judge fare classification against actual fare tap timestamps in returned JSON, not only the requested query time.

journeys.purpose: One minute before the morning peak boundary; inspect actual first tap time.
At the morning peak boundary; inspect actual first tap time.
One minute before the morning peak ends; inspect actual first tap time.
At the morning peak end; inspect actual first tap time.
One minute before the afternoon peak boundary; inspect actual first tap time.
At the afternoon peak boundary; inspect actual first tap time.
One minute before the afternoon peak ends; inspect actual first tap time.
At the afternoon peak end; inspect actual first tap time.

scenarios.name: weekend-early-shift-arrival
scenarios.purpose: Model a job shift requiring arrival by 02:30 on Saturday and Sunday. Compare arrive-by planner results and depart-at 02:30 results; capture night bus routes, walking transfers, route times and fare components.

journeys.purpose: Saturday, arrive by 02:30 (e.g. a 03:00 shift with 30-minute buffer).
Sunday, arrive by 02:30 (e.g. a 03:00 shift with 30-minute buffer).
Saturday, leave at or after 02:30; compare service availability.
Sunday, leave at or after 02:30; compare service availability.

scenarios.name: weekend-late-shift-return
scenarios.purpose: Check the return direction after a late Saturday or Sunday shift. Query the actual return departure date/time; do not reuse the outbound route or fare.

journeys.purpose: Saturday late return, departing Canary Wharf at 23:00.
Sunday late return, departing Canary Wharf at 23:00.
After-midnight return following a Sunday shift; confirm which calendar date the query must use.

scenarios.name: daylight-saving-overlap
scenarios.purpose: The UK clocks go back on this Sunday. Query the repeated local 01:30 and inspect whether Journey Planner results/tap timestamps identify an offset or select one occurrence. Record ambiguity as a limitation if the API cannot distinguish both local times.
